task.title: cut-release.sh fails on a moved desktop-latest tag
task.description:
scripts/cut-release.sh fetches with `git fetch --quiet --tags origin main` (line ~123) and fails with "could not fetch main and tags from origin" when any local tag no longer matches the remote. desktop-latest is a rolling tag the desktop publisher moves on every desktop release, so this fails for anyone who fetched it once and then a desktop release shipped: git refuses to clobber an existing tag without --force, the whole fetch is reported as failed, and the script stops before cutting anything. Hit on 2026-10-07 cutting v0.6.0-rc4; the fix by hand was `git fetch --force origin refs/tags/desktop-latest:refs/tags/desktop-latest`.

Make the fetch tolerate rolling tags: fetch main and the vX.Y.Z tags the script actually reasons about, and refresh desktop-latest (and any other known rolling tag) with --force or leave it out of the fetch entirely; the release tags themselves must never be force-fetched silently, since a moved v* tag is the kind of thing the script should refuse. Say in the failure message which ref was rejected rather than reporting the whole fetch. Cover it in scripts/cut_release_test.go with a local bare remote whose desktop-latest has moved past the clone's copy. Check scripts/setup-dev-env.sh and plan-release.sh for the same fetch shape.
